Anyway, so far it's been a mixed bag. I'm liking the customisation and the more personalised game experience with custom difficulty and all, but the game itself is pretty lacklustre. As of the completion of mission 2 a few things stand out to me the most.

-The AI

The AI is either aimbotting and hits every shot it takes the moment you step out of cover (snipers especially) or cannot see you when you're crouching literally at it's knees. There is barely any in between and it almost ruined the experience for me at times.

-The map design

The maps feel almost claustrophobic, especially mission 1, where you can't move through or hide in incredibly thin bushes and are railroaded to running often 40+ meters around hedgerows and stupid walls that you for some reason cannot vault, coupled with weird terrain that you can relatively easily get stuck on. I'm hoping since I've only completed mission 1 and 2 that this is just an issue in those examples.

-The visuals

The game kinda looks like shit. The textures and lighting are all *fine* but the anti-aliasing implementation really genuinely hurts my eyes at times. That bundled with the fact that it runs at just over 100fps (ultra, 1440p) on my 3070ti and lacks *any* DLSS implementation at all is grating, although considering the job they did with AA it might be a good thing after all that they didn't implement DLSS. FSR 1.0 is there, though. For some reason.

-The bugs

I know it's day 1 but.. come on. The x-ray camera doesn't really work right a lot of the time, enemies just ignore shots at some angles (an infantryman i encountered was manning an mg42 and shrugged off 12 headshots in the first mission) and killing some enemies breaks others pathing. It's kinda sad that this is the state of almost every newly released game these days, but i trust these issues will be ironed out over the next couple patches.

-On the other hand, the good

I still like the game so far and despite the issues i have with it, i'm having fun. that being said, i cannot particularly recommend the game in its current state due to the aforementioned issues, especially at the price point they are presenting. The classic SE gameplay loop is still as good as ever (it wouldn't have survived like 7 games if it wasn't) and the new customisation options are pretty cool, but the game has pretty big issues, most of which I'm hoping get patched in the near future, but some I'm more worried about being permanent dampers on the overall experience.

Sniper Elite 5 gives me exactly what I want from a sniper game: big maps, careful planning, ridiculous long shots, and the beautiful horror show that is the X-ray kill cam.

The best part of these games is always the setup. Finding a good vantage point, tagging enemies, watching patrols, planning the route, holding your breath, and waiting for that perfect shot. When it lands, it feels so satisfying. Horrible for the enemy’s organs, great for my dopamine.

This one feels smoother and more polished than the older entries. The maps are fun to explore, there are different ways to approach objectives, and I like having room to be tactical instead of being shoved down one path. You can sneak, sabotage, distract, trap, snipe, or completely mess up and turn the whole mission into a loud little disaster.

The stealth is still the heart of it for me. I love clearing areas carefully, moving through cover, hiding bodies, timing shots with sound, and pretending I am a calm professional instead of someone who just panicked because one guard turned around too fast.

And yes, the kill cam remains disgusting art. The game did not need to show me bones, lungs, eyeballs, and testicles being punished in slow motion, but here we are, respecting the craft.

Sniper Elite 5 is tense, satisfying, and extremely easy to lose time in if you enjoy stealth, sniping, and making one bullet ruin someone’s entire afternoon.

Sniper Elite 5 takes a step forward from 4 in many instances, yet takes a step back in others creating an awkward sidestep in gameplay. Multiple starting locations, kill targets, and weapon modification are parts of that step forward while the AI, removal of small QoL mechanics, and not-very-difficult authentic mode are parts of the step back. 

Maps are great with a variety of ways to tackle your objectives (helped by unlockable starting locations). They are a bit bigger than the maps in 4, but open areas seem a bit more sparse with some parts having just a handful of enemies. Level design wise, maps are open but not TOO open and have plenty of little spots to snipe some unexpecting enemies, just like in 4. AI has some problems, especially with verticality. Sometimes the enemy won't even check on your last known position, other times it's on par with 4's AI. Mixed in with the downgrade in "authentic" mode, it's just not as challenging as 4's authentic. Doesn't mean it's not challenging!, But if you're looking for something akin to authentic in 4, it's not quite there sadly. Kill targets is something I LOVE. That, paired with the challenges from 4 (why'd you get rid of them??), would make for some TASTY replayability. And having iron sights is MILES better than what 3 and 4 had.

If you're somehow here for story, *I* thought it was a nice story and good characters for a game not focused on plot lmao

Now if the next game had the long shots and the weapon modification from 3, challenges, AI, utility items, and authentic (plus) from 4, and the multiple starts, kill targets, and iron sights from 5, it would be (imo) the perfect SE game. Or very close.

So is it worth it? YES, and so are the DLC missions. Get the base game and the two season passes on sale. While I miss the infinite pebbles and the crouch running (and honestly a bunch more) from SE4, SE5 is my favorite of the two. Somehow lol

After  trying The 4th, which I partly enjoyed, I gave a one more shot for the new Sniper Elite. 
It's been a second game from this series for me, and in my opinion the best of all by far.

[u] Personal thoughts: [/u]

What made me to feel good in this, is that Sniper Elite finally came to France, 1944. That is what I like about it. That is a proof you can make WW2 game still with very modern and solid gameplay, that won't be totally generic.
Surprisingly D-Day doesn't felt like before in this title.  It used to have in call of duty series but, here, SE 5 is one and only a non-multiplayer game like (Post-Scriptum, HLL) that allows you to explore open maps based on Normandy locations. Still having their own and new flavour.
And some maps are enough big to let you enjoy the Normandy from open perspective. What is enjoying too, the number of WW2 guns and their customization is beyond satisfying, and it isnt over-looked nor overdone. If you're a WW2 enthusiasts you can love this series, I'm glad the Normandy came to this series with fresh look. Possibly next game will head towards the Pacific as some hints can be found in the game or into the Ardennes, Belgium, but we will see...

[u] What game offers? [/u]

- large maps and long missions 
- good and fresh looking Normandy and D-Day setting
- replayability e.g. exploring map=unlocking new start locations ,or unlocking new objectives
- use of different paths and fight methods
- good gun customization
- plenty of weapons and attachments to use (smgs, assault rifles, sniper rifles)
- invasion mode in campaign - the enemy player, playing as Wehrmacht's sniper tries to eliminate and stop you, or you can play to stop someone's missions
- multiplayer - with no run'gun cod like, just sniping , no crossing to run, very nice like in Ghost Warrior Games.

[u] What it doesn't offer? [/u]

- not all maps are that super big, half of them is in standard size
- only a couple missions where u play with other squad members or protect squads 
- still lone wolf game, doesn't involve you in that 'large' battle feeling

[u] Issues? [/u]

Game is very well optimized. As the minimum requirements are presented, you can still have 3gb or even less of VRAM, to enjoy the game. Tested on Gtx 750 ti, gtx 760 and finally on 1050ti. Graphics are really nice. Sometimes but much rarely, u can spot dead bodies to glitch in textures and not properly collide with some terrain objects. Not too often.
Sniper Elite 5 is really great game from the series. Though I spent good hours in this game, I feel it should have more missions as there are 8 (basic edition)- however pretty long to complete them 100%.

[u] Any improvements? [/u] 

- new possibilities of enemies AI, they aren't that stupid like before in SE Afrika (what I have heard before) or  you have to respect enemies in open engagement even on easy difficulty and plan your tactic.
- new movement and shot animations, 
- new audio effects: gun shots are extremely good, it's well made that silenced rifles are still loud, which is correct in real life.
- longer missions and more items to use, as well plenty explore and to find in loot.

[u] Conclusion: [/u]

Though I spent good hours in this game, I feel it should have more missions as there are 8- however very long to complete, and each location looks completely different. Apparently SE5 is the best from the series, still it is being updated with new content. The best game to grab from the series. If they make next part in the Pacific Theater it would be total epicness.
